editorial.titleTr: North Korea Threatens with Advanced Weapons While South Korea-U.S. Allied System Faces Major Setbacks
summaryTr: North Korea conducted a show of force with short-range ballistic missiles and drones.
It demonstrated capabilities to strike forward outposts, K9 self-propelled guns, and U.S. tanks.
The lack of interoperability in the Korea-U.S. combined defense system was pointed out as a serious problem.
editorial.bodyTr: North Korea staged a military demonstration by publicly releasing footage of short-range ballistic missile launches and various drone attacks. The regime showcased its strike capabilities through images of attacks on front-line outposts, K9 self-propelled howitzers, and mock targets of American tanks. The commander of U.S. Forces Korea emphasized that the South Korea-U.S. combined defense system faces significant obstacles due to insufficient interoperability, and stressed the need to transition from Kill Chain to Kill Web.

editorials.titleTr: Japan's Parliament Cuts Seats While Korea's National Assembly Maintains Lawmakers' Privileges
summaryTr: Japanese Parliament agrees to reduce proportional representation seats by 31
Reflecting population decline, push to cut seats from 500 to 434
South Korea's National Assembly maintains only privileges, deepening political distrust
editorials.bodyTr: Japan's ruling and opposition parties have agreed on a political reform plan to reduce the proportional representation seats in the House of Representatives by 31, and have decided to process it during the extraordinary Diet session. Japan has been reducing House seats from 500 to 465 to reflect population decline, and is now attempting to change to a system of 434 seats. The editorial points out that South Korea's National Assembly has deepened political distrust by repeatedly ignoring demands to reduce seats and privileges while increasing legislative salaries and expanding staff.

editorials.titleTr: New housing developments in Seoul metropolitan area must avoid becoming mere bedroom communities
summaryTr: The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport announced plans to supply 76,700 new residential lots across six areas in the Seoul metropolitan region.
While the target move-in date is 2033, questions are being raised about feasibility due to delays in third-phase new towns and resident opposition.
Transportation measures and job base expansion are necessary to prevent the areas from becoming bedroom communities while pursuing urban regeneration in parallel.
editorials.bodyTr: The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport has announced a plan to supply 76,700 new residential lots across six locations including Gimpo and Goyang. The government has set the first move-in date for 2033, but doubts about the pace have grown due to delays in the third new city project and resident resistance. To prevent traffic congestion and the creation of a bedroom community, transportation measures and job infrastructure must be supplemented, while Seoul should simultaneously pursue urban supply through redevelopment projects.

editorial.title: [사설] 대통령의 ‘목숨줄’, SNS 아닌 국민 삶에 있다
editorial.body: 입력 업데이트 종합 38면 2026.10.31 00:34 2026.10.31 00:30 2026.10.30 23:18 이재명 대통령이 각종 국정 현안과 정치 이슈에 관한 입장을 SNS 개인 계정에 집중적으로 올리고 있다. 이 대통령이 지지율 하락을 겪으며 잠시 잠잠했던 ‘SNS 정치’가 훨씬 증폭된 강도로 되살아나는 형국이다. “SNS는 목숨줄 같은 것”이라고까지 표현한 것은, 언론은 물론 친여 혹은 여권 내부 인사들까지 나서 SNS 자제를 조언한 것에 대한 단호한 거부 의사 표시로 들린다. 이 대통령이 쏟아내는 SNS 메시지는 사안의 핵심을 간명하게 전달하는 경우도 있지만, 부정확한 내용을 포함하거나 갈등을 부추기는 등의 문제점을 드러내는 사례도 적지 않다. 다문화 가족 산모의 공공산후조리원 입소 순위에 불만을 표하는 보수 성향 온라인 커뮤니티 글을 자신의 SNS에 공유한 게 대표적 사례다. 이 대통령은 “다문화 가족들이 피해를 입지 않는 것을 넘어 우대까지 할 필요성이 큰지, 우대 제도 폐지가 필요한지 등을 검토하겠다”고 적었다. 그런데 다문화 가족과 함께 입소 2순위에는 5·18민주유공자, 북한이탈주민 보호 대상 등도 들어있다. 세부 조건을 대통령이 미리 챙겨보았다면 ‘다문화 가족’만 콕 집어 ‘폐지’를 언급하진 않았을 것이다. “이주 노동자들은 소득을 전부 본국에 송금하기 때문에 한국 경제에 크게 도움이 안 된다”는 국무회의 발언에 대한 진보 성향 일간지의 보도를 왜곡이라 반박한 SNS도 마찬가지다. 대통령의 발언은 이주 노동자들의 본국 송금보다 국내 소비가 훨씬 많다는 정부 통계와도 맞지 않는다. 이 대통령이 언론 보도를 비판한 논리를 적용하면, 대통령은 자신의 발언으로 상처 받았을 이주 노동자들에게 사과하고 정정하는 게 옳다. 이재명 대통령이 28일 청와대에서 열린 국민생명안전위원회 제2차 전체회의에 참석해 자료를 살펴보고 있다. 청와대사진기자단 SNS란 매체는 즉흥적·즉시적 속성 때문에 효능도 있지만 부작용의 리스크도 크다. 대통령의 SNS가 매일 쏟아지는 수많은 SNS 중의 하나로 그친다면 별 문제가 아닐 수도 있다. 그러나 이 대통령의 SNS 메시지는 천금의 무게를 가진 정책 지시로 받아들여져 소관 부처가 우선 순위 상위에 두고 신속하게 후속 조치를 내놓는 게 상례다. 만일 대통령이 SNS에 부정확한 정보에 기반한 설익은 아이디어나 정책 방향을 밝히면 국정 운영에 큰 혼선과 부담을 줄 수밖에 없다. 더구나 이를 걸러내야 할 부처 장관들이나 청와대 참모들 다수가 ‘예스맨’들로 포진되어 있다는 평을 받고 있는 게 현실 아닌가. SNS 알고리즘이 자극적이고 진영 논리에 치우친 콘텐트를 적극 노출하며 확산하는 구조인 것도 경계해야 한다. 대통령이 특정 지지층이나 특정 커뮤니티의 게시물을 자주 공유하면 의도치 않더라도 사회적 통합은 어려워지고 대립과 혐오를 조장하게 될 수 있다. 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령이 SNS를 통해 보여준 정치 양태를 세계는 지켜봐 왔다. 트럼프 대통령은 제도권 언론을 ‘가짜 뉴스’로 매도하고 지지층을 향한 메시지를 던지며 즉흥적으로 정책을 뒤집거나 외교 상대국을 자극하기도 했다. 이 대통령은 SNS 정치의 부작용을 가볍게 여겨선 안 된다. 대통령 손에서 나오는 글자는 개인의 의견 표명이 아니라 국민 전체의 운명과 직결된 공적 구속력을 가진다. 성남시장이나 경기도지사에겐 그래도 될 지 모르나 대통령에게 SNS가 ‘목숨줄’이 되어선 곤란하다. 대통령이 수호해야 할 것은 자신의 정치생명이 아니라 국민의 삶이다. 이 대통령이 진정으로 ‘모두의 대통령’을 지향한다면 스마트폰을 내려놓는 걸 진지하게 검토하기 바란다. 양식 있는 국민이 원하는 건 ‘SNS 정치’가 아닌 ‘숙의의 정치’이기 때문이다.

summary: 이재명 대통령이 SNS 정치를 강화하며 지지층 결집에 나섰다.
부정확한 정보와 특정 진영 게시물 공유로 사회 통합을 해친다.

editorial.stance: 대통령은 정치생명 보호가 아닌 국민 삶 중심의 숙의 정치로 돌아가야 한다.
editorial.titleTr: Editorial: The President's Lifeline Lies in People's Lives, Not Social Media
summaryTr: President Lee Jae-myung has intensified SNS politics to rally his support base.
Sharing inaccurate information and partisan posts undermines social cohesion.
The president's SNS activities cause policy confusion and damage trust in government initiatives.
editorial.bodyTr:
President Lee Jae-myung is intensively posting his positions on various state affairs and political issues through his personal SNS account. This marks a resurgence of 'SNS politics,' which had quieted somewhat as the president experienced declining approval ratings, now amplified to a much greater degree. His characterization of SNS as a "lifeline" appears to be a firm rejection of calls for SNS restraint—not only from the media but also from pro-government insiders and figures within the ruling party. The SNS messages the president issues sometimes convey the essence of issues clearly, but there are numerous cases revealing problems such as inaccurate content or inflammatory rhetoric. A prime example is when the president shared on his SNS a post from a conservative-leaning online community expressing dissatisfaction with the admission order for multicultural families at public postpartum care centers. The president wrote, "We will review whether there is a strong need to provide preferential treatment beyond simply preventing multicultural families from suffering harm, or whether we need to abolish the preferential system." However, alongside multicultural families in the second admission tier are also 5.18 democratic activists, North Korean defectors under protection, and others. Had the president reviewed the detailed conditions beforehand, he would not have singled out 'multicultural families' and mentioned their 'abolition.' The same applies to his SNS post rebutting a progressive daily newspaper's report as distortion regarding his cabinet meeting remark that migrant workers do not greatly benefit the Korean economy because they send all their income back to their home countries. The president's statement contradicts government statistics showing that domestic consumption by migrant workers far exceeds their remittances to their home countries. If the logic the president used to criticize media reports were applied to himself, it would be appropriate for him to apologize to and correct his statement for migrant workers who would have been hurt by his remarks.

SNS as a medium has effectiveness due to its spontaneous and immediate nature, but it also carries substantial risks of side effects. If the president's SNS posts were merely one among the countless SNS messages flooding out daily, it might not be a major problem. However, the president's SNS messages are typically accepted as policy directives with the weight of gold, with relevant ministries placing them at the top of their priorities and promptly issuing follow-up measures. If the president discloses half-baked ideas or policy directions based on inaccurate information through SNS, it inevitably creates major confusion and burden in state governance. Moreover, is it not the reality that many of the cabinet ministers and presidential aides who should filter this out are criticized for being 'yes-men'? The structure in which SNS algorithms actively expose and spread provocative content tilted toward factional logic must also be monitored. If the president frequently shares posts from specific supporter groups or particular communities, social integration becomes difficult, even if unintended, and it risks fostering confrontation and hatred.

The world has watched the political conduct displayed by U.S. President Donald Trump through SNS. President Trump branded mainstream media as 'fake news,' sent messages to his supporters, and sometimes impulsively reversed policies or provoked foreign counterparts. This president must not take lightly the side effects of SNS politics. Words coming from the president's hand do not represent individual opinion but carry public binding force directly linked to the fate of the entire nation. This may have been acceptable when he was mayor of Seongnam or governor of Gyeonggi Province, but SNS should not become a 'lifeline' for the president. What the president must protect is not his own political life but the lives of the people. If this president truly aspires to be a 'president for all,' we urge him to seriously consider putting down his smartphone. What discerning citizens want is not 'SNS politics' but 'deliberative politics.

editorials.titleTr: Editorial: The President's Lifeline Lies in People's Lives, Not Social Media
summaryTr: President Lee Jae-myung has intensified SNS politics to rally his support base.
Sharing inaccurate information and partisan posts undermines social cohesion.
The president's SNS activities cause policy confusion and damage trust in government initiatives.
editorials.bodyTr:
President Lee Jae-myung is intensively posting his positions on various state affairs and political issues through his personal SNS account. This marks a resurgence of 'SNS politics,' which had quieted somewhat as the president experienced declining approval ratings, now amplified to a much greater degree. His characterization of SNS as a "lifeline" appears to be a firm rejection of calls for SNS restraint—not only from the media but also from pro-government insiders and figures within the ruling party. The SNS messages the president issues sometimes convey the essence of issues clearly, but there are numerous cases revealing problems such as inaccurate content or inflammatory rhetoric. A prime example is when the president shared on his SNS a post from a conservative-leaning online community expressing dissatisfaction with the admission order for multicultural families at public postpartum care centers. The president wrote, "We will review whether there is a strong need to provide preferential treatment beyond simply preventing multicultural families from suffering harm, or whether we need to abolish the preferential system." However, alongside multicultural families in the second admission tier are also 5.18 democratic activists, North Korean defectors under protection, and others. Had the president reviewed the detailed conditions beforehand, he would not have singled out 'multicultural families' and mentioned their 'abolition.' The same applies to his SNS post rebutting a progressive daily newspaper's report as distortion regarding his cabinet meeting remark that migrant workers do not greatly benefit the Korean economy because they send all their income back to their home countries. The president's statement contradicts government statistics showing that domestic consumption by migrant workers far exceeds their remittances to their home countries. If the logic the president used to criticize media reports were applied to himself, it would be appropriate for him to apologize to and correct his statement for migrant workers who would have been hurt by his remarks.

SNS as a medium has effectiveness due to its spontaneous and immediate nature, but it also carries substantial risks of side effects. If the president's SNS posts were merely one among the countless SNS messages flooding out daily, it might not be a major problem. However, the president's SNS messages are typically accepted as policy directives with the weight of gold, with relevant ministries placing them at the top of their priorities and promptly issuing follow-up measures. If the president discloses half-baked ideas or policy directions based on inaccurate information through SNS, it inevitably creates major confusion and burden in state governance. Moreover, is it not the reality that many of the cabinet ministers and presidential aides who should filter this out are criticized for being 'yes-men'? The structure in which SNS algorithms actively expose and spread provocative content tilted toward factional logic must also be monitored. If the president frequently shares posts from specific supporter groups or particular communities, social integration becomes difficult, even if unintended, and it risks fostering confrontation and hatred.

The world has watched the political conduct displayed by U.S. President Donald Trump through SNS. President Trump branded mainstream media as 'fake news,' sent messages to his supporters, and sometimes impulsively reversed policies or provoked foreign counterparts. This president must not take lightly the side effects of SNS politics. Words coming from the president's hand do not represent individual opinion but carry public binding force directly linked to the fate of the entire nation. This may have been acceptable when he was mayor of Seongnam or governor of Gyeonggi Province, but SNS should not become a 'lifeline' for the president. What the president must protect is not his own political life but the lives of the people. If this president truly aspires to be a 'president for all,' we urge him to seriously consider putting down his smartphone. What discerning citizens want is not 'SNS politics' but 'deliberative politics.

editorial.title: Deepening asymmetry
editorial.body: Soaring chip profits and GDP gains mask strains in Korea's domestic economy A nation can grow rich on paper even as its people feel poorer. South Korea’s latest figures tell two different stories: Export earnings are soaring, but household fortunes are lagging. An artificial intelligence-driven surge in chip demand has sent output and corporate earnings to unprecedented levels. Yet the gains are concentrated in a handful of exporters, leaving much of the domestic economy struggling to keep pace. On Tuesday, the Bank of Korea reported that gross domestic product grew 1 percent from the previous quarter in July-September, lifting cumulative growth for the first three quarters to 3.6 percent. Real gross domestic income rose 18.8 percent year-on-year, its largest gain since 1977, and per capita gross national income is expected to exceed $40,000. SK hynix on Wednesday reported third-quarter operating profit of 83.33 trillion won ($62.36 billion), up 632 percent from a year earlier. Samsung Electronics followed on Thursday with 107.44 trillion won, a 783.1 percent jump. The scale of this windfall is extraordinary. The question is how much it says about the health of the wider economy. The domestic data is far less buoyant. Private consumption fell 0.2 percent in the quarter. Consumer confidence weakened, and average monthly employment gains over the first nine months were the lowest in six years. Small businesses are under pressure, too. The delinquency rate on loans from the Industrial Bank of Korea reached 1.04 percent, its highest since records began in 2011. The composition of the boom helps explain the divide. About 78 percent of the recent increase in semiconductor exports came from higher prices rather than larger volumes. The AI infrastructure race has given Korea’s memory chip leaders extraordinary pricing power and record earnings. Samsung’s semiconductor division generated nearly all its operating profit, offsetting an 800 billion won loss in consumer electronics and mobile operations. SK hynix reported an operating margin of 80 percent and said long-term agreements cover more than half of its production capacity for 2027-28. The scale of the boom also distorts the national picture. Semiconductor exports accounted for nearly half of total shipments in September. The BOK has warned that a slowdown in US technology giants’ AI spending could sharply reduce chip exports and shave 0.4 percentage point off growth. Despite record earnings, recent swings in Samsung and SK hynix share prices show how heavily valuations depend on continued demand, particularly as Chinese competitors catch up. Advanced manufacturing creates enormous value without generating jobs at the pace Korea needs. The share of young workers moving from precarious employment into permanent jobs fell from 3.5 percent in 2014-19 to 1.6 percent in 2023-24. When large firms favor experienced hires and smaller employers lack the means to invest, young people can be shut out of the prosperity their work helps create. Dividends and bonuses may support consumption at the margin, but the gains remain concentrated among shareholders and employees of a handful of large firms. The government should raise productivity and encourage investment beyond semiconductors. It should also remove regulations that prevent new platforms and innovative services from expanding. Labor reform must open routes into stable jobs for young people and narrow the divide between secure positions at large firms and precarious work elsewhere. Public support should target vulnerable households and retraining. Financial oversight must also contain household debt, which constrains spending and leaves families exposed to higher borrowing costs. Record profits and rising GDP are genuine achievements. Whether the economy is healthy depends on whether households and smaller firms share in the gains. Policymakers have had ample warning of the divide. The test is whether they can broaden the sources of income and employment before chip prices retreat. summaryTr: 한국의 반도체 호황은 가계 소비와 일자리 증가가 기록적인 기업 이윤에 크게 미치지 못하는 경제 침체를 덮어가고 있다.
삼성과 SK하이닉스의 extraordinary 수익은 거래량이 아닌 AI 기반 가격 결정력에서 비롯되며, 중소기업과 청년 근로자들이 소외되고 있다.
정책 입안자들은 반도체 이상으로 성장을 다각화하고 보다 광범위한 번영이 가계와 소규모 기업에 도달하도록 보장해야 한다.
editorial.bodyTr:
칩 수익과 GDP 성장이 한국 국내경제의 긴장을 가리고 있다

국가는 국민이 더 가난해지고 있다고 느껴도 종이 위에서는 부자가 될 수 있다. 한국의 최근 통계는 두 가지 다른 이야기를 보여준다. 수출 수익은 급증하고 있지만, 가계의 재정 상황은 뒤처지고 있다. 인공지능 주도의 칩 수요 급증이 생산과 기업 수익을 사상 최고 수준으로 끌어올렸다. 그러나 그 성과는 소수의 수출업체에 집중되어 있으며, 국내경제의 대부분은 이에 발맞추기 위해 고투하고 있다.

한국은행이 화요일 발표한 자료에 따르면 7월-9월 분기에 국내총생산이 전 분기 대비 1% 성장했으며, 첫 3개월 누적 성장률은 3.6%로 집계됐다. 실질 국민총소득은 전년 대비 18.8% 증가해 1977년 이후 최대 증가폭을 기록했으며, 1인당 국민총소득은 4만 달러를 넘을 것으로 예상된다.

SK하이닉스는 수요일 3분기 영업이익이 83조 3300억 원(62조 3600만 달러)으로 전년 대비 632% 증가했다고 발표했다. 삼성전자는 목요일 107조 4400억 원으로 783.1% 증가했다고 뒤따라 발표했다. 이러한 횡재의 규모는 정상을 벗어난 것이다. 문제는 이것이 광범위한 경제의 건강 상태에 대해 얼마나 많은 것을 말해주는가 하는 것이다.

국내 통계는 훨씬 덜 낙관적이다. 그 분기에 민간소비는 0.2% 감소했다. 소비자 신뢰도가 약화했으며, 지난 9개월간 평균 월간 고용 증가는 6년 만에 최저를 기록했다. 소기업들도 압박을 받고 있다. 한국산업은행의 대출 연체율은 1.04%로 2011년 통계 작성 이후 가장 높은 수준에 도달했다.

붐의 구성이 이 분열을 설명하는 데 도움이 된다. 최근 반도체 수출 증가의 약 78%는 거래량 증가가 아닌 가격 상승에서 비롯됐다. AI 인프라 경쟁은 한국의 메모리칩 선도 기업들에 비상한 가격 결정력과 기록적 수익을 안겼다. 삼성의 반도체 부문이 거의 모든 영업이익을 창출했으며, 소비자전자 및 모바일 사업의 8000억 원 손실을 상쇄했다. SK하이닉스는 80%의 영업이익률을 기록했으며, 2027-28년 생산 능력의 절반 이상이 장기 계약으로 보장되어 있다고 밝혔다.

붐의 규모는 또한 국가 통계를 왜곡한다. 9월 반도체 수출이 전체 출하액의 거의 절반을 차지했다. 한국은행은 미국 기술 거대 기업들의 AI 지출 감소가 칩 수출을 급격히 줄이고 성장률에서 0.4포인트를 깎아낼 수 있다고 경고했다. 기록적 수익에도 불구하고, 삼성과 SK하이닉스 주가의 최근 변동은 특히 중국 경쟁사들이 따라잡고 있는 가운데 평가가 지속적인 수요에 얼마나 크게 의존하는지를 보여준다.

첨단 제조업은 한국이 필요로 하는 속도로 일자리를 창출하지 않으면서 엄청난 가치를 생산한다. 불안정한 고용에서 정규직으로 이동하는 청년 근로자의 비중은 2014-19년 3.5%에서 2023-24년 1.6%로 하락했다. 대기업들이 경험 많은 신입사원을 선호하고 소기업들이 투자할 여력이 없을 때, 청년들은 자신의 노동이 창출하는 번영에서 배제될 수 있다.

editorials.title: Deepening asymmetry
editorials.body: Soaring chip profits and GDP gains mask strains in Korea's domestic economy A nation can grow rich on paper even as its people feel poorer. South Korea’s latest figures tell two different stories: Export earnings are soaring, but household fortunes are lagging. An artificial intelligence-driven surge in chip demand has sent output and corporate earnings to unprecedented levels. Yet the gains are concentrated in a handful of exporters, leaving much of the domestic economy struggling to keep pace. On Tuesday, the Bank of Korea reported that gross domestic product grew 1 percent from the previous quarter in July-September, lifting cumulative growth for the first three quarters to 3.6 percent. Real gross domestic income rose 18.8 percent year-on-year, its largest gain since 1977, and per capita gross national income is expected to exceed $40,000. SK hynix on Wednesday reported third-quarter operating profit of 83.33 trillion won ($62.36 billion), up 632 percent from a year earlier. Samsung Electronics followed on Thursday with 107.44 trillion won, a 783.1 percent jump. The scale of this windfall is extraordinary. The question is how much it says about the health of the wider economy. The domestic data is far less buoyant. Private consumption fell 0.2 percent in the quarter. Consumer confidence weakened, and average monthly employment gains over the first nine months were the lowest in six years. Small businesses are under pressure, too. The delinquency rate on loans from the Industrial Bank of Korea reached 1.04 percent, its highest since records began in 2011. The composition of the boom helps explain the divide. About 78 percent of the recent increase in semiconductor exports came from higher prices rather than larger volumes. The AI infrastructure race has given Korea’s memory chip leaders extraordinary pricing power and record earnings. Samsung’s semiconductor division generated nearly all its operating profit, offsetting an 800 billion won loss in consumer electronics and mobile operations. SK hynix reported an operating margin of 80 percent and said long-term agreements cover more than half of its production capacity for 2027-28. The scale of the boom also distorts the national picture. Semiconductor exports accounted for nearly half of total shipments in September. The BOK has warned that a slowdown in US technology giants’ AI spending could sharply reduce chip exports and shave 0.4 percentage point off growth. Despite record earnings, recent swings in Samsung and SK hynix share prices show how heavily valuations depend on continued demand, particularly as Chinese competitors catch up. Advanced manufacturing creates enormous value without generating jobs at the pace Korea needs. The share of young workers moving from precarious employment into permanent jobs fell from 3.5 percent in 2014-19 to 1.6 percent in 2023-24. When large firms favor experienced hires and smaller employers lack the means to invest, young people can be shut out of the prosperity their work helps create. Dividends and bonuses may support consumption at the margin, but the gains remain concentrated among shareholders and employees of a handful of large firms. The government should raise productivity and encourage investment beyond semiconductors. It should also remove regulations that prevent new platforms and innovative services from expanding. Labor reform must open routes into stable jobs for young people and narrow the divide between secure positions at large firms and precarious work elsewhere. Public support should target vulnerable households and retraining. Financial oversight must also contain household debt, which constrains spending and leaves families exposed to higher borrowing costs. Record profits and rising GDP are genuine achievements. Whether the economy is healthy depends on whether households and smaller firms share in the gains. Policymakers have had ample warning of the divide. The test is whether they can broaden the sources of income and employment before chip prices retreat. 국가는 국민이 더 가난해지고 있다고 느껴도 종이 위에서는 부자가 될 수 있다. 한국의 최근 통계는 두 가지 다른 이야기를 보여준다. 수출 수익은 급증하고 있지만, 가계의 재정 상황은 뒤처지고 있다. 인공지능 주도의 칩 수요 급증이 생산과 기업 수익을 사상 최고 수준으로 끌어올렸다. 그러나 그 성과는 소수의 수출업체에 집중되어 있으며, 국내경제의 대부분은 이에 발맞추기 위해 고투하고 있다.

한국은행이 화요일 발표한 자료에 따르면 7월-9월 분기에 국내총생산이 전 분기 대비 1% 성장했으며, 첫 3개월 누적 성장률은 3.6%로 집계됐다. 실질 국민총소득은 전년 대비 18.8% 증가해 1977년 이후 최대 증가폭을 기록했으며, 1인당 국민총소득은 4만 달러를 넘을 것으로 예상된다.

SK하이닉스는 수요일 3분기 영업이익이 83조 3300억 원(62조 3600만 달러)으로 전년 대비 632% 증가했다고 발표했다. 삼성전자는 목요일 107조 4400억 원으로 783.1% 증가했다고 뒤따라 발표했다. 이러한 횡재의 규모는 정상을 벗어난 것이다. 문제는 이것이 광범위한 경제의 건강 상태에 대해 얼마나 많은 것을 말해주는가 하는 것이다.

editorial.body: 현대자동차가 3분기 실적을 발표하며 "매월이 컨틴전시(비상경영) 체제"라고 밝혔다. 수요 둔화와 글로벌 교역 경쟁, 거시경제 불확실성, 지정학 리스크가 겹친 상황에서 비상 상황처럼 하루하루를 버티고 있다는 절박함의 표출이다. 지난 29일 발표된 회사의 3분기 연결 매출은 45조1102억원으로 전년 동기보다 3.4% 줄고, 영업이익은 2조6772억원으로 소폭..
summary: 현대차가 '매월이 컨틴전시'라며 비상경영 체제 돌입을 선언했다.
수요 둔화와 글로벌 경쟁, 지정학 리스크가 동시에 압박하고 있다.
3분기 매출 45조원으로 전년비 3.4% 감소, 영업이익도 소폭 하락했다.
editorial.stance: 경기 악화 속 회사 위기 상황을 노조도 함께 인식하고 현명한 대응이 필요하다.

summaryTr: Actor Choi Bul-am passed away at the age of 87.
